fields.AN_Notes: Four policy prompts (restrooms, snow removal, office temperature, business-trip expenses), each submitted 50 times to ChatGPT (GPT-4) and Microsoft Copilot in neutral, male, female and partly non-binary or young-mother variants; themes retained at a 70 percent threshold. Prompts serve as research instrument; the role framing of the prompts ('If you were the city mayor') is not described as a technique, so AN_Prompt_Techniques = None. Other_Task: AI as policy advisor for workplace and municipal policy design, outside social work. Non-binary employees are an analysed group, coded as Sexual_Orientation_Identity; intersectionality is invoked in the discussion but not analysed. Harm types from the work's own results: male default (Exclusionary_Norms), omission of women's and non-binary needs in neutral prompts (Erasure), baby-changing only in women's restrooms read as care stereotype (Stereotyping). Mitigation only proposed in the conclusion: audits, Human-in-the-Loop and multidisciplinary teams (Organisational_Process), curated gender-balanced datasets (Pre_Processing), fine-tuning (In_Training), equity principles 'not just in prompts' (Prompt_Practice). Gender understanding: the analysis carries non-binary variants as own categories; Connell's view of gender relations as institutionally embedded is applied to restroom design. Theory frame: Tronto's ethics of care, Young's justice as inclusion, capabilities approach, Connell, Grosz, feminist spatial planning, design justice.

fields.AN_Notes: Maximum perspective diversity extraction from GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, GPT-3, Llama3-70b-chat and Mixtral on Social-Chem-101, Change My View, a hate-speech dataset and Moral Stories, compared with crowd-worker opinions. The proposed criteria-based diversity prompting (generate stance, criteria words, then reasons) is coded Thought_Generation; one-shot and five-shot demonstrations are ICL; the step-by-step recall prompting iteratively extends the opinion list and has no separate family. Prompting is both the proposed practice and the instrument. Diversitaet rests on perspective diversity as the central object, linked by the authors to overlooked minority perspectives; no social group is analysed, so AN_Bias_Axes = None (crowd-worker race and education appear only as sample demographics in the limitations and appendix). Bias appears only as bias towards a dominant viewpoint, hence Bias_Ungleichheit teilweise and AN_Bias_Definition Implicit_Only. Mitigation: criteria-based prompting against a single dominant opinion, evaluated by semantic and perspective diversity scores and a human preference study (AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated, limited to this intervention). Other_Task: generation of diverse opinions and data for subjective NLP tasks such as annotation and data augmentation, outside social work. The values theory (Rokeach) frames opinion formation, not gender or bias, so AN_Theory_Reference = No.

fields.AN_Notes: Interpretative qualitative visual and intersectional analysis of 180 SDXL images from 18 deliberately minimal prompts (privilege and discrimination, ideology, everyday scenarios) on micro, meso and macro levels, complemented by a review of online and academic sources. Prompts serve as research instrument; minimal prompts were chosen on purpose, no technique is used or recommended, so AN_Prompt_Techniques = None; the discussion recommends that users be conscious of the prompts they use (Recommended_Practice). AN_Task = None: the work audits default image outputs without a professional application task; creative and design use is context only. Axes are coded from the own image analysis: gender, skin tone and ethnicity, disability and body size, age, wealth and class, immigrant/refugee versus citizen, Global North cultural hegemony, heteronormativity and absent non-binary representations; Intersectional from the micro-level analysis of the white, adult, able-bodied, heteronormative masculine default and single-axis diversification. Religion was excluded from the scope by the authors. Harm types: stereotyping, exclusion of feminine, non-binary and disabled representations (Erasure), white able-bodied masculine default (Exclusionary_Norms), reductionist portrayal of cultures and Global South as poor (Misrepresentation). The violent-symbol finding (confederate flag) concerns imagery, not language, so Toxicity is not coded. Mitigation only proposed within algorithmic reparation: curated training data (Pre_Processing), conscious prompting by users (Prompt_Practice), responsible designers, diverse teams, regulation and criminal culpability (Organisational_Process). Fairness = nein, since fairness research is mentioned only in passing and the work frames its proposals as reparation rather than fairness criteria. Gender definition from footnote 2, which replaces man/woman by heteronormative feminine/masculine representations to avoid reinforcing the binary norm.

fields.AN_Notes: Prompt tuning (trainable soft prompt embeddings concatenated to the input of frozen BERT and RoBERTa) as a debiasing method, trained on 159 gender-profession templates with a KL-divergence loss towards the average distribution across groups, evaluated on SEAT and StereoSet with language-modelling score and pseudo-perplexity. Prompting is the proposed mitigation practice; soft prompt tuning belongs to none of the technique families, and in-context learning appears only as motivation, so AN_Prompt_Techniques = None. Mitigation stage: the work places its intervention at inference ('additional information at inference') with model weights frozen, coded Intra_Processing, and the intervention is a change to the prompt input, coded Prompt_Practice; it is evaluated with mixed results (on par with state of the art, second to INLP on BERT). Axes: gender is the target; race and religion are measured as side effects on StereoSet. Harm type: stereotyping measured by the StereoSet stereotype score; the Gallegos harm list in the introduction is background and not coded. Gender is operationalised as he/she and male/female name pairs without a definition. Bias is determined technically by the stereotype score near 50 percent and by the reference distribution averaged across groups. Generative_KI = ja because the work frames its object as large language models, although the tested models are encoder-only. Fairness = ja because the work is a debiasing method with a fair and unbiased output as target and bias metrics as evaluation.

fields.AN_Notes: Audit study with 42 prompt templates in five scenarios (purchase, chess, public office, sports, hiring) and 40 first names perceived as Black or white and male or female, 100 repetitions each, on GPT-4, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama-3-70B, Mistral Large and PaLM-2. Prompts are the research instrument; the three context levels (low, qualitative, numeric anchor) are prompt-design variations, not a named technique family, so AN_Prompt_Techniques = None. Mitigation: the numeric anchor in the prompt is evaluated and removes name-based disparities in most scenarios, qualitative context has inconsistent effects (Prompt_Practice, Evaluated); audits at deployment and implementation are recommended (Organisational_Process, Proposed). Intersectional is coded under the AN_Bias_Axes rule because Black female-perceived names yield the worst outcomes, although the authors state that their analysis does not equate to an evaluation of intersectionality. Harm types: Indirect_Discrimination because names act as proxies in advice on offers, salaries and chances (the codebook anchor), and Stereotyping because the authors attribute the disparities to encoded stereotypes, including the reversed basketball case. Other_Task: advice to laypeople in negotiation, hiring salary offers, election and sports predictions, outside social work. Gender is operationalised through male- and female-perceived names without definition. Bias is defined through the legal pair of disparate treatment and disparate impact, which also frames the interpretation (theory reference). Feministisch = nein because the work explicitly declines an intersectional analysis and offers no structural gender critique.
